Definition: an unclean bird, perhaps the parrot (from its irascibility)
BiblicalUsage: The word appears twice, in the same list both times: among the unclean birds, after the stork, the heron after her kind, and the lapwing, and the bat. It is the heron — a wading bird, named from its irascibility, the anger in its cry — and the law counts it unclean, not to be eaten.
TheologicalSignificance: One bird in two lists carries no doctrine of its own; its weight is the list — the clean and the unclean set apart, and the heron on the unclean side.
